newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen Group acquires California funeral firm.
newsitem.headline: Loewen Group acquires California funeral firm.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc., the target of a hostile takeover bid by rival funeral home operator Service Corp. International, said Friday it agreed to acquire Rose Hills Co. Inc. of Los Angeles for $240 million.

Vancouver-based Loewen is teaming up with Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund L.P. of New York, to acquire the cemetery and mortuary operations and assets of Rose Hills Co. and The Rose Hill Memorial Park Association.
Rose Hills Memorial Park is the largest cemetery in North America.

Loewen, North America's second-largest funeral home company, said the Rose Hill deal was in the works before Service Corp. launched its unsolicited $43 a share bid, worth $2.8 billion, on Tuesday. Houston-based Service Corp. is North America's biggest funeral home company.
Loewen founder and Chairman Ray Loewen said Rose Hill will add to the company's earnings.

"This transaction ... is part of Loewen's long-term growth plan to acquire strategic operators consisting of larger urban properties as well as small, family-owned funeral homes and cemeteries," Loewen said in a statement.
This is the second time Loewen has linked up with Blackstone in a major acquisition.
Last June, Loewen and Blackstone joined forces to buy Prime Succession Inc., the largest privately held funeral home operator in the United States, for $320 million.
Under the terms of the deal, Loewen and Blackstone will form a new company to acquire the Rose Hills operations.
Loewen will integrate its 14 funeral homes and two combination funeral home/cemetery operations in California's Los Angeles and Orange counties into the new company.
Blackstone and its affiliates will be the major shareholders and control the board of directors in the new venture. But Loewen will have the option to buy Blackstone's interest after four years.
The deal is expected to close by mid-December.
